# Kyoto 4-Day Trip Plan: Apr 10–13, 2026

A temple-focused, walking-friendly itinerary that keeps transfers short and centers your stay around a major train hub. I’m assuming you want a comfortable mid-range hotel, mostly public transit and walking, and one higher-end dinner for two.

## Best Areas to Stay for Short Transfers

- **Kyoto Station area**: Best for arrival/departure ease, JR access, and simplest day trips. Slightly less atmospheric, but the most efficient base.
- **Gion / Higashiyama**: Best for temple walks, traditional streets, and easy access to Kiyomizu-dera, Yasaka Shrine, and Philosopher’s Path connections.
- **Shijo / Kawaramachi**: Best balance of dining, shopping, and transit. Very convenient for buses/subway and walkable evenings.
- **Karasuma / Oike**: Quiet, central, and efficient for subway travel. Good if you want a calmer mid-range hotel without sacrificing access.

## 4-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: Arrival + Eastern Kyoto walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, and keep the first half-day light.
- **Afternoon:** Walk the **Gion → Yasaka Shrine → Maruyama Park → Kiyomizu-dera** corridor.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon:** Walk the **Gion → Yasaka Shrine → Maruyama Park → Kiyomizu-dera** corridor, Kyoto, Japan
- **Dinner:** Casual Kyoto-style set meal near Gion or Higashiyama; save the nicer dinner for Day 3.
- **Transfer note:** Stay on foot as much as possible; use one taxi only if needed from station to hotel.

### Day 2: Arashiyama temples and river area
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Early start to **Arashiyama** for the bamboo grove before crowds.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Tenryu-ji**, stroll the river, and continue to **Okochi Sanso Garden** or **Iwatayama** if energy allows.
- **Dinner:** Back near Kyoto Station or Shijo for an easy return and simple meal.
- **Transfer note:** One direct train route out and back keeps this day efficient.

### Day 3: Philosopher’s Path + central temples + nice dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Morning:** Start at **Ginkaku-ji** and walk the **Philosopher’s Path**.
- **Afternoon:** Continue to **Nanzen-ji** and nearby sub-temples if you want a slower pace.
- **Dinner:** Book your **one nice dinner** tonight in **Gion, Kawaramachi, or central Kyoto**.
- **Transfer note:** This is your best low-stress “walk day” with a compact route.

### Day 4: Central Kyoto temples + departure buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Nijo Castle** or **Nishiki Market** depending on your departure time.
Media: Alt=Morning:** Visit **Nijo Castle** or **Nishiki Market** depending on your departure time, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Final shopping, café stop, and return to hotel for bags.
- **Dinner:** If you fly out later, keep this as a flexible light meal near Kyoto Station.
- **Transfer note:** Choose one central sight only to avoid rushing before departure.

## Cost Estimate for 2 Adults

| Category | Estimate | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Mid-range hotel, 3 nights | **$450–$750** | Near Kyoto Station, Gion, or Shijo |
| Local transit | **$40–$90** | Mostly subway, JR, and occasional taxi |
| Food and drinks | **$260–$420** | Mix of casual meals plus one nicer dinner |
| Temple/admission fees | **$40–$90** | Depends on how many paid sites you enter |
Media: Alt=| Temple/admission fees | **$40–$90** | Depends on how many paid sites you enter |, Kyoto, Japan
| Nice dinner for two | **$80–$180** | Kaiseki, seasonal set menu, or upscale izakaya |
| Miscellaneous | **$60–$120** | Snacks, coffee, small purchases, buffers |
| **Total** | **$930–$1,650** | Fits within your **$1,800** budget |

## Recommended Budget Split

- **Hotel:** Aim for **$150–$230 per night** total for 2 adults.
- **Daily food:** Plan around **$60–$100 per day** for both of you.
- **Transit:** Keep it lean by staying near a train station and grouping sights by area.
- **Splurge moment:** Put the nicer dinner on Day 3 so it feels like a highlight, not a logistics burden.

## Quick Actions
